source-dispositions.evidence: Primary-authored KTZ catalog. Genuine labeled photos on pages 11, 12, 15 and 19 were extracted. Page 11 TMZh image remains held because photographic origin is uncertain. TM35 photo is real, but power and LV are unknown; overview wording also conflicts with TM tap-changer terminology. Technical sections mostly contain dimensional drawings.
Official dedicated reactor page gives ROM60000/525. The stated 60000 kVAr, 525/sqrt(3) kV, 198 A and 1531 Ohm match the canonical ROM60000/500 record. The photo is a genuine single-phase reactor.

Distinct factory photograph of separate single-phase reactor tanks. Article names ROM60000/525. The image does not establish an individual unit nameplate. Three single-phase tanks are not a single three-phase reactor.

All 36 PDF pages were rendered into a contact sheet and text inspected. Factory, storage, staff, project and component photographs have no new unambiguous designation captions for remaining missing families.

All 22 gallery photos were downloaded and visually inspected. They show real factory equipment and processes but have no individual model captions or readable designation plates. Specific homepage project-captioned photos are already in the frozen first pass.
Four distinct oil, dry and storage photos appear in repeated crops. No image-specific voltage, railway or large-power designation evidence. Cropped and resized versions do not count separately.
The exact AOMZh product image is a technical drawing. TRDNS35 and TDN10/11 photos show tall bushings and lack image-specific Alageum attribution. Titles alone cannot establish the photographed model.
All 21 gallery thumbnails were inspected. They show switchgear, cabinets, substation buildings and assembly work, not the target transformer bodies.

Four high-voltage cutouts are reused across TD, TDNS, TDS and TDN listings. One is positively identified as TDNS in the primary KTZ catalog. TM listings repeat one front view across ratings and voltages. These cannot safely fill missing model families.

Latest listing and pages 2–5 were read. Relevant 35 kV catalog links were followed. Low-voltage TMG/OMP leads were passed to the parent; those pages were subsequently confirmed to lack product photos. No missing power-family photo was identified.

Accessible TMTN page and real factory photo were inspected. No readable maker identification ties the image to Alageum/KTZ. Filename includes 220 while listing says 110, and the site exhibits generic image reuse. Held. Previously denied URLs were not retried.
Page is in a 6/10 kV category and photo has compact bushings. Text mentions 35 kV but does not establish that the pictured unit is 35 kV. Not used for TMG35.
Explicit Alageum OMZh27.5 kV page uses the same shot as KTZ catalog xref526, with watermarks added. Provenance corroboration only; not a second photo.
One watermarked photo is shared by a joint TDNS/TRDNS 10–25 MVA page. No readable designation or split-winding evidence distinguishes which model is pictured. Not counted as TRDNS.

ELMO-Alageum title says TRDNS25000/35, but the photo is a small conventional TM distribution transformer with conservator and no visible large-power/RPN construction. Asset filename references TSL630/20. Rejected.
Dated supplier news explicitly names ATDCTN250000/220/110 for Batys. Genuine factory photo bears Alageum/AsiaTrafo branding and 250 MVA overlay. One composition, counted once.
HTML title names TM6300/35/6.3, but retrieved content contains no product image. Also incompatible with the 10 kV TM4000–6300 family.
Returned a 195-byte Site Unavailable page. Indexed text mentions TRDN280000/220 for Ekibastuz, but the photo cannot be verified. No blocked asset was retried.
Direct public URL returned HTTP403. It was not retried. Independently published EPR and manufacturer sources were examined instead.
Official reference-list text verifies projects such as TDTN25000/220 at Josaly and ATDCTN63000/220, but tables do not assign identities to generic factory photographs.

Independently published mirror appeared in search before the Telegram preview was attempted. Browser text fetch had cache miss; direct public page returned HTTP403. No retry, asset call, proxy or alternate mirror attempted. TRDN280000/220 remains an unresolved inaccessible-photo lead.
